patients.summary: Elementary school teacher with lifelong atopy (eczema, allergic rhinitis) and recurrent HSV-1 cold sores, who had intraoperative anaphylaxis as a child and again at a 2025 nevus excision, later traced to latex. HSV keratitis of the right eye in October 2025 healed without sequelae.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT, ESTABLISHING CARE

32-year-old woman, elementary school teacher, transferring from her previous primary office. No acute complaints today. Wants one place to call when her allergies or skin act up.

HISTORY
Eczema since she was a toddler. These days it is mostly hands and the creases of the elbows in winter, and the mometasone ointment keeps it quiet; she uses it a few days at a time, not continuously. Moisturizes with a fragrance-free cream.
Allergies: itchy watery eyes and congestion every spring with the trees, plus a year-round stuffy nose she was told was dust mite. Daily fluticasone, cetirizine on bad days.
Cold sores since her teens, roughly two or three a year. Keeps valacyclovir at home and starts it at the first tingle.
At 8 she had her tonsils and adenoids out and had a severe allergic reaction in the OR. Her mother was told it was anaphylaxis but no one ever told them what caused it. She has never had testing. No reactions to any medicine since that she knows of.

PSH: T&A age 8 (reaction as above).
Meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment BID PRN; cetirizine 10 mg daily PRN; fluticasone nasal 1 spray each side daily; valacyclovir 1 g at prodrome then 1 g 12 h later.
Allergies: dust mite and tree pollen (rhinitis). No known drug allergies.
Family: mother asthma and hay fever; father eczema; younger sister also gets cold sores.
Social: teaches elementary school. Never smoked. A glass of wine once or twice a month. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative except as above. No wheeze or asthma symptoms of her own.

EXAM
Well appearing. HEENT: TMs clear, mild pale nasal turbinates, oropharynx clear, lips without lesions. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: a few faint dry patches at both antecubital fossae, no excoriation or weeping. No edema.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Atopic dermatitis, quiet right now. Continue mometasone in short bursts, daily emollient.
2. Allergic rhinitis, perennial with spring flares. Continue fluticasone daily and cetirizine as needed.
3. Recurrent herpes labialis. Episodic valacyclovir, refills on file.
4. History of anaphylaxis during childhood surgery, cause unknown. Advised she tell any surgeon or dentist about it before a procedure.
5. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids; one-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, which she agrees to. Requesting records from her prior office, including her last Pap and immunizations. PHQ-2 negative.
Lab draw Monday morning. Follow up for a physical next year or sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your Recent Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lisa, everything from Monday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were both negative. Nothing to change. Nice meeting you last week.

documents.title: Records From Prior Primary Care Office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from the patient's previous primary care office, 41 pages, 2016 to 2022. Abstracted:
- Cervical cytology with HPV co-test 06/2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion, HPV negative. Next due 2026.
- Tdap 03/2019.
- Problem list: eczema, allergic rhinitis, recurrent cold sores, remote anaphylaxis during childhood surgery.
- Medications match what she brought to her first visit.
- Allergies listed as dust mite and tree pollen.
No childhood surgical records in the packet. Placed in chart for PCP review.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after school for vaccines. No fever or illness today. Screening questions negative; history of childhood OR reaction noted, no prior vaccine reactions. Influenza vaccine left deltoid, bivalent COVID booster right deltoid. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction. VIS given.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request for mometasone 0.1% ointment, 45 g; old prescriber is her prior office. Routed to PCP. Approved, 45 g with 2 refills, transferred to our prescriber.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Hands cracking and itchy since the holidays, worse with all the handwashing in the classroom and the dry heat at school. Elbow creases flaring too. Using the mometasone most nights for about a week, which helps, but it comes back when she stops. No oozing, no crusting, no fever. Sleep a little broken by the itch.
O: Vitals as charted. Dorsal hands with dry, lichenified erythematous plaques and a few fissures over the knuckles; both antecubital fossae with mild erythema and scale. No vesicles, no honey crust, no pustules.
A: Atopic dermatitis, winter flare, hands and flexures. No sign of infection.
P: Mometasone twice daily for two weeks, then weekends only for a few weeks. Heavy plain ointment after every wash and cotton gloves over it at night. Keep a fragrance-free hand cream at her desk. If the hands are not better in three weeks, message me and we can talk about dermatology.

documents.title: Allergy Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the trees are out and I am a mess. Could you send refills of the nasal spray and the cetirizine? My hands are fine now, the gloves trick worked. Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Allergy Refills
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Done, both sent with a year of refills. During the worst of the pollen it is fine to take the cetirizine every day rather than as needed. Glad the hands settled.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient called to cancel tomorrow's 4:00. End-of-year events at school, and she says she feels well. Will book her physical for September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREVENTIVE VISIT

Interval: good year. One mild cold sore in the spring that she caught early with valacyclovir. Hands stayed decent since the winter flare. Allergies typical for the spring, controlled on the spray. No ER visits, no new meds.

Current meds: mometasone 0.1% ointment PRN, cetirizine 10 mg PRN, fluticasone nasal daily, valacyclovir episodic.
Allergies: dust mite, tree pollen. NKDA.
Social: back in the classroom. Never smoker, rare alcohol. Walking most evenings.

ROS negative in detail. Periods regular.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Pleasant, well. HEENT normal, lips clear. Neck without adenopathy or thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen benign. Skin with faint dryness of the knuckles only. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright.

A/P:
- Adult preventive care: PHQ-2 0. Pap/HPV co-test was negative in 2021; next one due 2026. Tdap 2019, current. Flu and updated COVID given today.
- Atopic dermatitis, controlled. Same plan; start the night-glove routine early this winter.
- Allergic rhinitis, stable.
- Recurrent cold sores, infrequent. Valacyclovir refilled.
- Remote anaphylaxis, cause unknown. Reminded her to flag it before any procedure.
- CBC, CMP and lipids drawn today. Physical again in a year.

documents.title: Physical Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lisa, labs from Thursday's physical were all normal, cholesterol included. See you next year, or anytime you need us.
